extraction.name: Prompted Textures Dataset (PTD)
extraction.description: A new texture dataset spanning 246,285 images across 56 texture classes, created using an extensible methodology that leverages text-to-image models to generate high-quality, diverse, and specific texture images.
extraction.creator: Blaine Hoak and Patrick McDaniel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was generated by producing texture-specific prompts using combinations of artistically-informed descriptors across 56 texture classes. These prompts were used as inputs to Stable Diffusion model pipelines to produce corresponding texture images. A three-stage refinement process was then applied to filter the images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were generated using the Stable Diffusion model from HuggingFace based on constructed text prompts.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-stage refinement process was applied to filter the generated images: (1) frequency filtering to remove object-like images by retaining the top 80% of images with the highest frequency cutoff threshold, (2) patch variance filtering to eliminate homogeneous images by removing the bottom 20% with the lowest mean patch variance, and (3) CLIP score filtering to ensure prompt alignment by removing the bottom 20% of images with the lowest CLIP scores.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The labels/annotations are the prompts used to generate the images. Prompts were structured by combining one word from each category in standard English adjective order: {Artistic} {Spatial} {Color Enhancer} {Color} {Texture}. This produced 96,768 unique prompts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A human evaluation study was conducted with 9 participants who evaluated 100 images each. Participants rated the overall quality of the image and how well the image represented the provided descriptor on a scale of 1 to 5. The evaluation confirmed that the refinement process yielded a 3.4% increase in quality and a 4.5% increase in representativeness.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: CLIP (used for scoring and filtering image-prompt alignment)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset contributes valuable resources for advancing interpretability, bias analysis, and robustness in machine learning by enabling large-scale analyses of texture bias and model trustworthiness.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The generation process showed variations across texture classes. Textures that more often appear in common objects (e.g., hairy, flaky) tended to have better quality scores, while simpler but more structured textures (e.g., grid, polka-dotted) tended to have worse scores. Additionally, certain word pairings (e.g., 'muted' or 'earthy' with subtle textures) resulted in lower quality images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Stable Diffusion models are not explicitly designed to create textures, so object-like images can arise. Furthermore, the model's safety filter was overly sensitive to texture data, flagging up to 60% of initially generated images (especially for descriptors like 'paisley') as NSFW. These flagged images were excluded from the final dataset.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Interpreting high-level features models learn, uncovering biases (specifically measuring texture bias and texture-object associations), and identifying security vulnerabilities (e.g., adversarial examples).
